newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds mixed, 15-yrs seen bought.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds mixed, 15-yrs seen bought.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities turned in a mixed performance on Tuesday, with 30-year paper losing ground versus Treasuries but 15-year spreads narrowing thanks to heavy buying, traders said.
"(A bank) bought about $1.5 billion," one trader said. "When he was done, the market came off a little."
By late afternoon, 30-year pass-throughs were off 1/32 to 3/2, while 15-year issues were just a touch higher.
The near-term outlook for 15-year paper appears bright, one trader said. "It still looks cheap, and the March/April roll is already well-bid," he said.
More broadly, traders said 8.0- and 8.5-percent 30-year collateral traded well. One trader said he expected the announcement of two new CMOs constructed from higher-coupon Ginnie Mae II paper.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 2/32 at 100-18/32, yielding 106 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac coupons were off 2/32 as well, at 100-13/32 and 100-18/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was off 1/32 at 100-19/32 to yield 6.42 percent.
